traps: Quarter vs first half: every headline number has a first-half twin ($37.57 billion net revenues, $12.26 billion net earnings, $38.51 diluted EPS, 21.7% ROE); the second-quarter figures are $20.34 billion, $6.63 billion, $20.98 and 23.5%.
Year over year vs sequential: net revenues rose 39% versus 2Q25 but 18% versus 1Q26, GBM 53% vs 22%, and diluted EPS compares with $10.91 (2Q25) and $17.55 (1Q26).
Goldman reports GAAP figures only here; labeling any EPS or earnings figure as adjusted or non-GAAP is wrong.
Diluted EPS is $20.98 and basic EPS is $21.27; net earnings are $6.63 billion while net earnings to common are $6,399 million.

The efficiency ratio (58.8% vs 62.0%) and effective tax rate (18.5%) are first-half figures, not quarterly; the tax rate is compared with 13.2% for the first quarter of 2026, not with a year-ago rate.
The roughly $965 million tax benefit from employee share-based awards, which added about $3.15 to diluted EPS, is a first-half item disclosed in a footnote, not a second-quarter adjustment.
No guidance or outlook figures are given; the conference call reference to discussing the outlook is not guidance.
The $5.00 dividend is the third-quarter dividend declared July 13, 2026, raised from $4.50; the $1.36 billion of dividends paid during the quarter is a separate figure.
Units: the earnings and segment tables are in millions, while the balance sheet, capital ratio, GCLA and AUS tables are in billions.
Investment banking fees of $3.40 billion in the text round the segment table's $3,395 million; the income statement's Investment banking revenue line is a different line at $3,400 million.
Platform Solutions fell on net markdowns recognized in net revenues on the Apple Card portfolio; provision for credit losses actually fell to $102 million from $384 million.
Balance sheet, capital ratios, AUS, GCLA and VaR are preliminary estimates.
